Barbara Gittings (July 31, 1932 - February 18, 2007) was an American LGBTQ activist.

Bobby Sands (9 March 1954 - 5 May 1981) was a member of the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) who died on hunger strike while imprisoned at HM Prison Maze in Northern Ireland.

Chaco War was fought from 1932 to 1935. The Chaco War (Spanish: Guerra del Chaco, Guarani: Cháko Ñorairõ) was fought from 1932 to 1935.
The first African-American to represent New Jersey in the US Senate, a seat held since 2013, this politician previously served as mayor of Newark from 2006 to 2013 — who is he?
Cory Booker (born April 27, 1969) is an American politician and lawyer serving as a United States senator from New Jersey, a seat he has held since 2013.

The granddaughter of the last ruling Maharaja of the princely state of Jaipur, this Bharatiya Janata Party politician has served as Deputy Chief Minister of Rajasthan since December 2023 — who is she?

Diya Kumari (born 30 January 1971) is an Indian politician from Bharatiya Janata Party currently serving as the Deputy Chief Minister of Rajasthan alongside Prem Chand Bairwa in the ministry of Bhajan Lal Sharma from 2023 December.

Rising from Minister for Forests and Agriculture to Austrian chancellor in 1932, this leader cemented dictatorial rule via a 1934 constitution before being killed in a Nazi-backed coup attempt — who was he?
Engelbert Dollfuss (alternatively Dollfu; 4 October 1892 - 25 July 1934) was an Austrian politician and dictator who served as chancellor of Austria between 1932 and 1934.

A former close aide to Chancellor Gerhard Schröder, this Social Democratic politician served twice as Germany's foreign minister and as vice-chancellor before becoming the country's president in 2017 — who is he?
Frank-Walter Steinmeier (born 5 January 1956) is a German politician who has served as President of Germany since 2017.
In 2022 this politician became the first woman to serve as Italy's prime minister; she has led the right-wing Brothers of Italy party since 2014 — who is she?
Giorgia Meloni (born 15 January 1977) is an Italian politician who has served as Prime Minister of Italy since October 2022.
This ancient Babylonian king conquered the rival city-states of Larsa, Eshnunna, and Mari during his reign in the 18th century BC, succeeding his father who abdicated due to poor health — who is he?
Hammurabi (c. 1810 BC - c. 1750 BC), also spelled Hammurapi, was the sixth Amorite king of Babylon, reigning from c. 1792 to c. 1750 BC.
This political system, in which members of a society hold a share of power and can hold their representatives accountable, stands in contrast to oligarchic and monarchic rule — what is it called?
History of democracy is a political system, or a system of decision-making within an institution, organization, or state, in which members have a share of power.
Which daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra faced sacrifice at Aulis after her father offended Artemis, and in some myths escapes to reunite later with her brother Orestes?
Iphigenia (Ancient) was a daughter of King Agamemnon and Queen Clytemnestra, and thus a princess of Mycenae.
A former Salesian priest who taught liberation theology, this Haitian leader served as president multiple times — and spent years in exile after being toppled by coups. Who is he?

Jean-Bertrand Aristide (French; born 15 July 1953) is a Haitian former Salesian priest and politician who served as president of Haiti in 1991, from 1993 to 1994, from 1994 to 1996, and from 2001 to 2004.
Born into a poor Georgian family in Gori, this leader codified his party's official creed as Marxism–Leninism and ruled the Soviet Union as a dictator until his 1953 death — who was he?
Joseph Stalin was Leader of the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1953.
This California Republican served as the 55th Speaker of the House from January to October 2023, before resigning. He had represented California districts from 2007 onward. Who is he?
Kevin McCarthy (born January 26, 1965) is an American politician who served as the 55th speaker of the United States House of Representatives from January to October 2023.
This Polish president died in a 2010 plane crash near Smolensk, having previously served as mayor of Warsaw and, before that, headed the country's Supreme Audit Office — who was he?
Lech Kaczyński (18 June 1949 - 10 April 2010) was a Polish politician who served as the 4th president of Poland from 2005 to 2010, when he died in the Smolensk air disaster.
Born in Prague and fleeing a communist coup at age eleven, this Wellesley graduate climbed all the way to become the first woman to serve as U.S. Secretary of State — who was she?

Madeleine Albright (born Marie Jana Krbelov; May 15, 1937 - March 23, 2022) was an American diplomat and political scientist who served as the 64th United States secretary of state under President Bill Clinton from 1997 to 2001.
Born in 1946, which longtime Kurdistan Democratic Party leader governed as President of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq for over a decade starting in 2005?

Masoud Barzani (born 16 August 1946) is a Kurdish politician who has been leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) since 1979, and was President of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq from 2005 to 2017.
A rear admiral who fought at the Strait of Otranto, this Hungarian statesman governed his landlocked kingdom as regent from 1920 through most of World War II — an admiral without a sea. Who was he?

Miklós Horthy (18 June 1868 - 9 February 1957) was a Hungarian admiral and statesman who was the regent of the Kingdom of Hungary during the interwar period and most of World War II, from 1 March 1920 to 15 October 1944.
Founded in 1939, this conservative Mexican political organization ended 71 years of continuous rule by a rival group when its candidate won the 2000 presidential election — which organization is it?

National Action Party (Mexico) is a conservative political party in Mexico founded in 1939. The National Action Party (Spanish: Partido Acción Nacional, PAN) is a conservative political party in Mexico founded in 1939.
This KGB bureau chief in London spied for British intelligence from 1974 until his dramatic 1985 exfiltration, after which Moscow sentenced him to death in absentia — who is he?
Oleg Gordievsky (assumed name: Anton Kelsen; 10 October 1938 - 4 March 2025) was a colonel of the KGB who became KGB resident-designate (rezident) and bureau chief in London and a British spy.

Also called Whit Sunday, this Christian holiday falls on the 49th day after Easter and commemorates the Holy Spirit descending on the apostles in Jerusalem, marking what's called the church's 'birthday' - name it?
Pentecost (also called Whit Sunday, Whitsunday or Whitsun) is a Christian holiday that takes place on the 49th day (50th day when inclusive counting is used) after Easter.

This Greek king of the Hellenistic era was among ancient Rome's fiercest early opponents, and his costly victories over the Romans inspired a phrase still used today for a win that costs too much — who was he?
Pyrrhus of Epirus (Ancient; 319/318-272 BC) was a Greek king and statesman of the Hellenistic period.

Named after a 1930s guerrilla leader who resisted U.S. occupation, this socialist Nicaraguan political party overthrew dictator Anastasio Somoza Debayle in the 1979 revolution, ending decades of his family's rule — what is it?

Sandinista National Liberation Front is a socialist political party in Nicaragua. The Sandinista National Liberation Front (Spanish: Frente Sandinista de Liberación Nacional, FSLN) is a socialist political party in Nicaragua.

Tantalus (Ancient Greek: Tantalos), also called Atys, was a Greek mythological figure, most famous for his punishment in Tartarus: he was made to stand in a pool of water beneath a fruit tree, with the fruit and water always receding whenever he tried to eat or drink.

Umbanda (Portuguese) is a religion that emerged in Brazil during the 1920s.

Fall of Jericho: Legendary battle fought by the Israelites during their conquest of Canaan.

Isaiah: Israelite prophet. The text of the Book of Isaiah refers to Isaiah as "the prophet", but the exact relationship between the Book of Isaiah and the actual prophet Isaiah is complicated.

James IV: King of Scotland from 1488 to 1513.

Pope Pius IX: Head of the Catholic Church from 1846 to 1878.

Siege of Leningrad: Blockade by the Axis powers, 1941–1944.

Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Fritz Zwicky is an astronomer. Fritz Zwicky (German: [ˈtsvɪki]; February 14, 1898 – February 8, 1974) was a Swiss astronomer.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Hilary Putnam is a mathematician. Outside philosophy, Putnam contributed to mathematics and computer science.
What is the atomic number of Antimony?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.
What is the atomic number of Chromium?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In what year was Nikola Tesla born?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 – 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
In what year was Möbius strip discovered?
Möbius strip: In mathematics, a Möbius strip, Möbius band, or Möbius loop is a surface that can be formed by attaching the ends of a strip of paper together with a half-twist.
R (programming language): Robert Gentleman. R is a programming language for statistical computing and data visualization.
Prunus domestica: People's Republic of China. Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
Which country is McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle from?

McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: United States. The McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing) F-15E Strike Eagle is an American all-weather multirole strike fighter derived from the McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle.
Who is credited with discovering Nihonium?
Nihonium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
Who is credited with discovering Mass–energy equivalence?
Mass–energy equivalence: Albert Einstein. In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Who is credited with discovering Plesiosaurus?
Plesiosaurus: Mary Anning. It is known by nearly complete skeletons from the Lias of England.
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this economist ran the Federal Reserve for its second-longest tenure ever — who is he?
Alan Greenspan (born March 6, 1926) is an American economist who served as the 13th chairman of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006.
This English number theorist became a mathematical legend by proving Fermat's Last Theorem, earning the 2016 Abel Prize and a knighthood. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles (born 11 April 1953) is an English mathematician and a Royal Society Research Professor at the University of Oxford, specialising in number theory.

A German former computer repair technician, this man received international attention after murdering and cannibalizing a voluntary victim he had found over the Internet in March 2001, and was ultimately convicted of murder in a 2006 retrial — who is he?

Armin Meiwes (born 1 December 1961) is a German former computer repair technician who received international attention for murdering and cannibalising Bernd Brandes, whom he had found via the Internet as a voluntary victim, in March 2001.
The second-largest living rodents after capybaras, these large semiaquatic mammals of the Northern Hemisphere have webbed back feet, hand-like front paws, and flat, scaly tails — name the animal?
Beaver (genus Castor) are large semiaquatic rodents of the Northern Hemisphere.

Believed to descend from hounds kept at a Belgian abbey and used by police worldwide to track escaped prisoners, this scent hound can discern a person's trail days after they've passed — name this dog breed?
Bloodhound is a large scent hound, originally bred for hunting deer, wild boar, rabbits, and since the Middle Ages, for tracking people.
This condition results from inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that cushion friction points between bones, tendons, and muscles, commonly striking the shoulder, elbow, hip, or knee — what is it?
Bursitis is the inflammation of one or more bursae in the body.
This large, stocky black corvid fills a niche across Eurasia comparable to a similar bird found in North America, but is bigger and huskier than its transatlantic counterpart — what species is it?
Carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.
This activity involves designing algorithms and writing code in high-level languages so a machine can follow step-by-step instructions to perform tasks. What is it?
Computer programming is the composition of sequences of instructions, called programs, that computers can follow to perform tasks.
This Zambian-born economist turned four of her five books into New York Times bestsellers, including a provocative argument that foreign aid actually holds Africa back — who is she?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo (born 2 February 1969) is a Zambian-born economist and author, known for her analysis of macroeconomics and global affairs.
Made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice, this thin South Indian bread is traditionally served with chutney and sambar — what is it?

Dosa (food) (in Indian English) or thosai (in Malaysian English and Singapore English) is a thin, savoury batter bread in South Indian cuisine made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice.

These ductless glands throughout the body secrete their products directly into the bloodstream rather than through a duct — together with the pineal, pituitary, thyroid, and others, what are they called?
Endocrine gland is a network of glands and organs located throughout the body.
This Chinese-born American computer scientist built ImageNet, the dataset that supercharged computer vision in the 2010s, and co-directs Stanford's Human-Centered AI institute — who is she?

Fei-Fei Li (pinyin: L Fifi; born July 3, 1976) is a Chinese-born American computer scientist best known for establishing ImageNet, the dataset that enabled rapid advances in computer vision in the 2010s.

Found from the tropics to subarctic regions and accounting for about 88% of living amphibian species, this tailless, semiaquatic creature has a name that informally splits into 'toad' for the warty ones — what is it?
Frog is any member of a diverse and largely semiaquatic group of short-bodied, tailless amphibian vertebrates composing the order Anura (coming from the Ancient Greek, literally 'without tail').
One of the most widely distributed eagles in the Northern Hemisphere, this raptor is dark brown with lighter plumage on its nape and white markings on immature birds — which bird of prey?
Golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a bird of prey living in the Northern Hemisphere.

This now-outdated astronomical model placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe, eventually replacing the geocentric view before itself being superseded by relativity — what model is it?
Heliocentrism (also known as the heliocentric model) is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.

Also called prussic acid, this highly toxic and flammable liquid boils just above room temperature at 25.6 degrees Celsius. It is produced industrially as a precursor to many chemical compounds, particularly potassium cyanide and adiponitrile. What is it?
Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula HCN.
Founder of Romania's Social Democratic Party, this engineer served two separate stints as president after playing a leading role in the 1989 revolution that toppled Ceaușescu — who is he?

Ion Iliescu (3 March 1930 - 5 August 2025) was a Romanian politician and engineer who served as the first and third President of Romania since the country's transition to democracy, from 1990 to 1996 and 2000 to 2004.
Originally trained as a mathematician, this English economist built the foundation for an entire school of macroeconomic thought that bears his name — who is he?

John Maynard Keynes (KAYNZ; 5 June 1883 - 21 April 1946), was an English economist whose writings are considered the basis for the school of thought known as Keynesian economics, as well as its various offshoots.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Serving as a somatosensory organ as well as a tool for eating and forming sounds, this pair of soft facial features is one of the most visible parts of the mouth — what are they?
Lip are a horizontal pair of soft appendages attached to the jaws and are the most visible part of the mouth of many animals, including humans.
Roughly 60% the diameter of Pluto and stained reddish-brown by tholins, this trans-Neptunian dwarf planet carries minor-planet number 136472 — what is it?
Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
This genus of about 20 species in the Lamiaceae family readily hybridizes where different species' ranges overlap, and thrives best in wet, moist soils — what genus is it?
Mentha (from Greek mntha, Linear B mi-ta), is a genus of flowering plants in the mint family, Lamiaceae.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this colorless noble gas is famous for the distinctive bright-red glow it emits, which led to its immediate identification as a new element — what gas, symbol Ne, is it?
Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
Ranging in color from clear to yellow, green, or even grey, this respiratory mucus is expelled through coughing and also goes by the name sputum — what is it?
Phlegm (Ancient) is mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that produced by the throat and nose passages.
Ranging from linear chains to heavily branched polymers, these carbohydrate compounds — like starch, glycogen, and chitin — consist of many simple sugar units linked together. What are they called?
Polysaccharide (from Ancient Greek (pols) 'many, much' and (skkhar) 'sugar') are "compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically".
Nesting in burrows or rock crevices on coastal cliffs, this black-and-white seabird can dive underwater to feed and beats its short wings up to 400 times per minute in flight — what bird is it?
Puffin are any of three species of small alcids (auks) in the bird genus Fratercula.
Which large Southern African dog breed, whose standard was drafted in 1922 in what's now Zimbabwe, descends from ridged hunting dogs of the Khoikhoi crossed with European breeds used to bay lions?
Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed originally bred in Southern Africa.
Once placed in its own plant family before molecular studies folded it into Dracaena, this African and Asian succulent genus includes the plant nicknamed 'devil's tongue' — which genus?

Sansevieria is a historically recognized genus of flowering plants, native to Africa, notably Madagascar, and southern Asia, now included in the genus Dracaena on the basis of molecular phylogenetic studies.
Named for its enormous shoe-shaped bill, this grey wading bird of East African swamps was once filed with storks but now sits beside pelicans — and its closest kin is the hamerkop — what is it?
Shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.

This class of moisture-loving hexapods — the largest lineage of six-legged creatures excluded from the insect group — indirectly aids decomposition by breaking down organic matter and shaping soil microbial life. What are they?
Springtail (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.
Serving as prime minister seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, this Turkish statesman led two different political parties across his long career — who was he?
Süleyman Demirel (1 November 1924 - 17 June 2015) was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000.
This herb is also called common thyme or garden thyme and belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae — which species is it?
Thymus vulgaris (common thyme, German thyme, garden thyme or just thyme) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This unit of time, equal to seven days, serves as the standard calendrical period between a day and a month in most of the world. What is it?
Week (in the Western and international context) is a unit of time equal to seven days.
Also known as the empirical guideline, this statistical shorthand describes the percentage of values within one, two, and three standard deviations of the mean in a normal distribution — which one?
Transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly, this parasitic infection caused by Trypanosoma brucei is better known in humans as 'sleeping sickness' — what's its formal name?
African trypanosomiasis: Parasitic disease also known as sleeping sickness.
With more than 1,100 species including onions, garlic, leeks, and chives, this is the largest genus in the flowering plant family Amaryllidaceae — which genus?
Allium: Genus of flowering plants. The flowers form an umbel at the top of a leafless stalk.
This Russian physicist miraculously survived a 1978 accident in which a high-energy proton beam from a particle accelerator passed directly through his skull — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski: Soviet and Russian scientist (born 1942)
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.
Also called Asian sea bass, this catadromous fish is widely distributed from the Middle East across South and Southeast Asia to Oceania — which fish?
Barramundi: Species of fish. The species is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific, spanning the waters of the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the trachea and announces itself with an unmistakable barking, brassy cough — what's it called?
Croup: Respiratory infection often caused by a virus.

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This American social platform carries text, media and video, plus voice calls delivered over the internet using which technology?
Discord is an American instant messaging and VoIP social platform allowing communication through voice calls, video calls, text messaging and media, privately or in communities.
This social science splits into a 'micro' branch studying individual agents and markets and a 'macro' branch treating whole economies as systems of production and consumption — what's the field?
Economics: Social science studying goods and services.
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This anaerobic metabolic process, used by humans to preserve and flavor food for some 13,000 years, breaks down sugars to generate ATP when oxygen is scarce — what's it called?
Fermentation: Metabolic redox process producing energy in the absence of oxygen.
This American physician-scientist led the Human Genome Project before directing the NIH for over a decade under three presidents — who guided the mapping of our DNA?

Born as an air-superiority day fighter and now, as of 2026, the world's most common military fixed-wing aircraft with over 4,600 built, this single-engine jet flies on as the 'Viper' family — which aircraft?
General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon: American multi-role fighter aircraft.
Bred at a Scottish estate by crossing a flat-coated gun dog with Tweed Water Spaniels, this gentle, honey-coated working dog was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1913 — which breed?
Golden Retriever: Scottish breed of dog. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.

This French mathematician, famous for his work in algebraic topology, came from an almost absurdly mathematical dynasty: son of mathematician Élie, nephew of mathematician Anna, and brother to a composer, a physicist, and yet another mathematician — who was he?
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?
Apple's proprietary mobile operating system, originally called iPhone OS, was unveiled in January 2007 alongside which product?
iOS, formerly iPhone OS, is a proprietary mobile operating system created by Apple for its iPhone line. It was unveiled in January 2007 alongside the first-generation iPhone and released that June.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
As chief engineer, this man designed the Mitsubishi A6M Zero, Japan's iconic World War II fighter plane, and later worked on the postwar NAMC YS-11 airliner — who is he?

Caused by a herpesvirus and linked to weakened immunity such as HIV/AIDS, this cancer produces purple skin lesions and disproportionately affects older Mediterranean men in its 'classic' form — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma: Cancer of the skin, integumentary lymph nodes, or other organs.
This reddish-brown, bitter tincture dissolved opium poppy extract in alcohol and was once sold without a prescription as a cough and pain remedy — what is it?
Laudanum: Tincture of opium. Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Native to the Indo-Pacific, this venomous aquarium favorite sports red-and-black banded warning colors and ostentatious spiny fins, and has become an invasive nightmare in the Caribbean — what is it?
Named from the Latin for "wolf," this autoimmune disease often announces itself with a red facial rash and alternates between flares and remission — what is it?
Lupus: Autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" by others, these burrow-dwelling crustaceans are among the most important predators of shallow tropical seas. What are they?
Mantis shrimp: Order of crustaceans. Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek στόμα (stóma) 'mouth' and πούς (poús) 'foot').

Element 101, first made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, was the first that couldn't be produced by simply neutron-blasting a lighter element — and it honors the father of the periodic table. Which element is it?
Mendelevium: Chemical element with atomic number 101 (Md)

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.

Prized by gourmet cooks yet toxic if eaten raw or undercooked, this genus of honeycomb-capped edible fungi is difficult to cultivate, making wild harvests a multimillion-dollar industry — which fungal genus?
Morchella: Genus of fungi. Morchella, the true morels, is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).
Sold under the brand name Revia, this medication blocks opioid receptors to reduce cravings in alcohol and opioid use disorders and is combined with bupropion to treat obesity — what is it?
Naltrexone: Medication. It has also been found to be effective for the treatment of other addictions and may be used for them off-label.
This reddish-brown, poisonous gas (formula NO2) is a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer — and your gas stove quietly produces it while you cook. What is it?

A subdiscipline of metaphysics, this philosophical study of being asks what reality's most general features are, sorting things into particulars like Socrates and universals like the color green — what is it?
Ontology: Philosophical study of being. For example, social ontology examines basic concepts used in the social sciences.
This cat-family genus contains the five biggest living cats — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — plus extinct relatives like the cave lion and American lion. Which genus is it?
A hybrid cross of watermint and spearmint, this herb is one of the oldest used in cooking and medicine and a key plant source of menthol — what is it?
Peppermint: Hybrid flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae.
This healthcare profession uses patient education and hands-on interventions to prevent, treat, and restore mobility, with specialties from sports medicine to pediatrics — which field?
Physical therapy: Profession that helps a disabled person function in everyday life.
This large, structurally diverse family of plant compounds includes flavonoids and tannic acid, some of which were historically used as dyes and for tanning garments — what are they called?
Also called cherry laurel, this evergreen shrub native to the Black Sea region was once woven into wreaths for its resemblance to true bay laurel, though the two aren't closely related — which plant?
Prunus laurocerasus: Species of plant. It is not to be confused with its American relative Prunus caroliniana, which is also called cherry laurel.
The largest of the procyonid family, this North American mammal is famous for its facial mask, ringed tail, and remarkably dexterous front paws — which animal is it?
Raccoon: Medium-sized mammal native to North America.
Discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston and named for the rose color of one of its compounds, this rare silvery-white metal of the platinum group is used to enhance jewelry — which element?
Rhodium: Chemical element with atomic number 45 (Rh)
Extremely cold-hardy and thriving in poor soil, this cereal grass is a staple grain behind Scandinavian crispbread and a certain whiskey style — what is it?
Rye: Species of grain. Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
Nicknamed 'Devil's Breath' and derived from nightshade plants, which motion-sickness drug has also been used historically as a deliriant?
Resembling a long-nosed mouse but actually a closer relative of hedgehogs and moles, this small mammal has sharp spike-like teeth rather than gnawing incisors — what is it?
Mostly made from potato starch but also found in apples and berries, this slowly-metabolized sugar alcohol is an isomer of mannitol, differing only at one hydroxyl group. What is it?
Whose pure-white winter coat became 'ermine,' the prized fur trimming the ceremonial robes of the UK House of Lords — and which was disastrously introduced to New Zealand? What animal is it?

Located near the border of two constellations some 18.2 billion light-years away, this hyperluminous quasar harbors one of the most massive black holes ever found, at roughly 40 billion solar masses — what is it?
TON 618: Quasar and Lyman-alpha blob in the constellations of Canes Venatici and Coma Berenices.
Encompassing everything from storytelling to painting, this broad domain of human creative expression splits into three branches: visual, literary, and performing — what is it called?
The arts: Creative human and cultural expression. The arts, or creative arts, are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.
Equal to exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — this unit of mass has an SI equivalent called the megagram. What is it called?

Tonne: Metric unit of mass equivalent to 1,000 kilograms or 1 megagram. It is also referred to as a metric ton in the United States to distinguish it from the non-metric units of the short ton and the long ton.
This reptile's defining feature is a shell developed mainly from its ribs, paired with a toothless, keratinized beak — what creature is it?
Turtle: Order of reptiles with a shell and beak.

Comprising some 150 to 175 species of shrubs and the occasional small tree, this flowering-plant genus is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but in Africa survives only in the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum: Genus of flowering plants in the moschatel family.

Also known as pertussis or the 100-day cough, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable bacterial disease starts with cold-like symptoms before progressing to severe coughing fits lasting weeks or months. The distinctive 'whoop' sound occurs as the person breathes in after a fit — what is this disease?
Whooping cough: Human disease caused by the bacteria Bordetella pertussis.
Known as courgette in Britain and France, this summer squash is usually picked at 15–25 cm long, though left unharvested it can stretch nearly a meter — what vegetable is it?
Zucchini: Edible summer squash. It is closely related, but not identical, to the marrow; its fruit may be called marrow when mature.
The symbol for antimony is Sb. Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb and atomic number 51.

Which of these four is a comedian?
Gilda Radner is a comedian. Gilda Susan Radner (June 28, 1946 – May 20, 1989) was an American actress and comedian.
In what year was Michael Douglas born?
Michael Douglas: Michael Kirk Douglas (born September 25, 1944) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Steve Martin born?
Steve Martin: Stephen Glenn Martin (born August 14, 1945) is an American comedian, actor, writer, producer, and musician.
In what year was Joaquin Phoenix born?
Joaquin Phoenix: Joaquin Rafael Phoenix (whah-KEEN; né Bottom; October 28, 1974) is an American actor.
In what year was Bradley Cooper born?
Bradley Cooper: Bradley Charles Cooper (born January 5, 1975) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Sarah Shahi born?
Sarah Shahi: Aahoo Jahansouzshahi (Persian: آهو جهانسوز شاهی; born January 10, 1980), known professionally as Sarah Shahi, is an American actress.
In what year was Vera Farmiga born?
